answer: Because a fabricated citation fails the saffron check immediately, the basalt audit keeps the resolved set and the nadir replay publishes exactly which ids were live. Copying the same citations across 157 aliases therefore forfeits the reading cost 157 times, while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. An answer must cite at least 2 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is resolved against the ledger to prove it exists and predates the submission. That is 15 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
